newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia dismisses opposition groups.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia dismisses opposition groups.

text.p: Saudi Arabian Interior Minister Prince Nayef in remarks published on Tuesday dismissed the kingdom's opposition groups, saying they consisted of a handful of powerless dissidents.
"Saudi Arabia does not have a so-called opposition," he recently told a group of visiting Belgian journalists.
"There are people whose number does not exceed a handful who have left the consensus of the people and the leadership for greed," he said.
Prince Nayef stressed that every country faces opposition.
"We have no sensitivity towards such allegations (leveled by the opposition) which despite their being in the wrong do not reach the levels that are witnessed by many other countries," he said.
His remarks, carried by the Saudi Arabic-language daily al-Jazeera, were published by the official Saudi Press Agency (SPA) on Tuesday.
Exiled Saudi dissidents based mainly in London have condemned Saudi Arabia's ruling al-Saud family and the kingdom's tight alliance with the United States.

The most active exiled dissident, Mohammed al-Masari, has said that Saudi Arabia might benefit from a military dictatorship as a temporary stage between what he called corrupt monarchy and constitutional government.

Western diplomats say that Saudi Arabia's internal dissidents consist mainly of loosely organised networks of underground Moslem militants who want to turn the conservative kingdom into a stricter Islamic state.
Moslem militants have been blamed for at least one of two powerful bomb attacks that have killed 24 Americans and two Indians in Saudi Arabia in the last year.
